Resolves #19488

The stale workflow keeps marking issues `stale` after 90 quiet days, but it can no longer close them: `days-before-issue-close: -1`, and the close message is gone. An issue now closes only on a triage verdict that cites what superseded it, as #15000's closure-honesty rule already requires.

Its file is renamed to `mark-inactive-issues.yml` (nothing referenced the old name), and the job to `mark-issues`. The job drops `pull-requests: write`, since PRs were already exempt (`days-before-pr-*: -1`). The stale message now tells the reader that triage follows, not a close.

Why now (measured 2026-10-09): 456 closed issues carry `stale`, 390 of them from one 2024 batch and 66 from 2025–2026. Fourteen open issues are marked `stale` now and would close around 2026-10-19, among them the blog-post tickets #9850, #9853 and #9854. Recovering the closed ones is #19489.

Evidence: L1 (a workflow config change; the YAML parses, and `actions/stale` documents `-1` as never closing) → L2 required for the scheduled-run behavior. Residual: AC-3 (the 14 stale issues still open after the next scheduled runs), Residual-Owner: #19489.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `days-before-issue-close: -1`; `close-issue-message` removed; the PR settings are unchanged (`-1`) |
| AC-2 | `days-before-issue-stale: 90` and `stale-issue-label: 'stale'` stay; the message names triage and says no automatic close follows |
| AC-3 | Post-merge: the 14 currently `stale` issues stay open through the next scheduled runs (01:30 UTC daily) |

## Deltas from ticket

- Least privilege: `pull-requests: write` is dropped, because the workflow touches no PR.

- The YAML parses (`js-yaml`), and a config check confirms `days-before-issue-close: -1` with no close message.
- The workflow runs only on its schedule, so its behavior is verified after merge (Post-Merge Validation).
